witnesses.provenance: Solana's PACKET_DATA_SIZE is 1,232 bytes -- the 1,280-byte IPv6 minimum MTU less a 40-byte header and an 8-byte fragment header. ProgramTest submits no packet and therefore cannot enforce it; Found31 is the defect class that produced (docs/evidence/GENERIC_FOUNDING_REACHABILITY_2026_08_26.md). So the campaign serialises each transaction itself and this witness compares the MEASURED extent against the stated limit. It is also what makes the tier's width restriction falsifiable: at N=258 this witness would fail on six of seven actions, which is why nothing at that width is recorded.

A null wire_bytes says the campaign did not measure. That is honest, and it is NOT a claim that the frame fits -- but the witness above takes a max over the recorded values, and a max over a list with nulls dropped would silently exclude exactly the transactions nobody measured. This pins that there are none.

witnesses.query: [.transactions[] | select((.label | test("at runtime width 1$")) | not)] | length | tostring
witnesses.provenance: The fast-lane packet clause is claimed at runtime width 1 and nowhere else. The campaign gates recording on the width rather than on a test name, so this witness is what stops a later test recording an N=258 transaction into a tier whose packet clause does not hold there. It reads the label the campaign emits from the authenticated ControllerRequestV2 and the width, not a hand-written string.

Solana's per-transaction maximum, and the number both General fixtures pass to set_compute_max_units and never adjust. TIERS.md forbids satisfying a gate with a diagnostic budget, so the limit the campaign requests is the protocol one.

The accelerator distinguishes TRANSPORT failure from a failure-atomic SEMANTIC refusal: a semantic refusal returns a typed refused AcceleratorAckV2 on a succeeding transaction, and only a transport failure raises a program error. Five of this campaign's hostile submissions are semantic and one -- the corrupted scratch page, whose whole-bank digest no longer matches the request -- is transport. If that distinction ever collapses, this number moves, and a campaign whose hostiles all started erroring would otherwise look exactly as green as one whose hostiles all started passing.

witnesses.query: [.transactions[] | select(.error != null) | select([.logs[] | select(contains("custom program error: 0xc003"))] | length == 0)] | length | tostring
witnesses.provenance: 0xC003 is GeneralAcceleratorSbfErrorV3::InvalidScratchBank, inside the band docs/decisions/0007 registers for this program (dclutch_refusal_registry::GENERAL_ACCELERATOR_REFUSAL_BASE, const-asserted in the program's own source). A refusal that reached a runtime error instead of the program's own taxonomy would satisfy the count above and mean something entirely different.

Solana's MAX_INSTRUCTION_STACK_DEPTH is 5. This campaign's shape is depth 2 -- the test caller at [1], the accelerator at [2] -- and the real Trading Hot path adds frames above it, so a campaign that quietly grew a level is worth seeing before that path is built.

TIERS.md requires a ProgramTest-backed tier to state which of the four fast-lane conditions it meets, and direct/ established the habit of stating them inside the evidence document beside the numbers they qualify rather than in prose in a file nobody opens. These four are the ones that are numbers; the other clauses are prose in the same block, which a reader can find because this witness proves the block is there.
